question: Should exec, process, active-session, and node-host tool results redact secret-shaped output by default, accepting that returned command output may no longer be byte-exact?
rationale: Both choices define a security and compatibility contract: default masking reduces agent-context exposure, while preserving raw output protects exact-output workflows; repository policy cannot select that tradeoff without owner intent.

options.title: Merge secure default
options.body: Accept redacted-by-default tool results with the structured marker and warning, and evaluate any explicit raw reveal control separately.

options.title: Require reveal control now
options.body: Hold the PR until it includes an explicit, narrowly authorized raw-output mode with tests for both safe-default and reveal behavior.

options.title: Preserve raw output
options.body: Decline result-boundary masking and pursue a different containment design that does not modify exec output bytes.

recommendation.title: Merge secure default
recommendation.body: Accept redacted-by-default tool results with the structured marker and warning, and evaluate any explicit raw reveal control separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent exec/process runtime history and the contributor's explicit decision request make this the strongest available owner signal.
